The Trinity is an interesting concept, precisely because on the surface it does not appear to be necessary. If you assume that there is one God, who is indivisible and perfect, why would you presume to regard him in three aspects?

I have to believe that the doctrine of the Trinity was driven by pre-existing beliefs among pagans, including the philosophical beliefs of the neo-Platonists, Hermetic philosophers, and the gnostics. I suspect the Trinity was an accomodation of existing philosophical concepts regarding the nature of God.

Jesus is regarded as God, but also son of God. He is, according to Catholic theology, both at the same time. The Holy Spirit appears to be a substitution or euphemism for God the Mother, who in Catholicism is personified by Mary, mother of Jesus. Christianity is a patriarchal religion, and could not acknowledge a mother goddess, but the influence of the Isis cult at Rome, as well as other goddess cults, was so strong, the Fathers of the early Church could not ignore it.

God the Mother was let in the back door of Christianity, as it were, in the form of the Holy Spirit, a concept that was well understood in the time the Acts of the Apostles was written. Of course it is closely related to the Jewish concept of the Shekhinah, which is understood by Jewish mystics to be female.

All this does not imply that the doctrine of the Trinity is incorrect. It is one way of looking at the nature of the divine source of all creation. In the Kabbalistic doctrine of emanations we see it in the Supernals, the three highest emanations that represent God the Father (Kether), God the Son (Chokmah) and God the Mother (Binah).

This is no different, at base, than the holy family of Osiris, Isis and Horus in Egyptian mythology. Details differ, but the underlying dynamic is the same. The nuclear family of father, mother and child is a lower, material reflection of the heavenly family of God the Father, God the Mother, and God the Child. As Hermes Trismegistus pointed out, "What is below is like what is above, and what is above is like what is below." It is enevitable that the expression of life in our material world in the form of the nuclear family should have its counterpoint in the supercelestial world of the gods. Hence, the doctrine of the Holy Trinity.
